subject: Halo Health — SLO qualification & stress test plan (batching / cache / quantization levers)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lee <anna.lee@halohealth.com>, Evan Torres <evan.torres@halohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Halo Health — SLO qualification & stress test plan (batching / cache / quantization levers)

Anna / Evan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope and what Redwood will validate in the stress run.

Call highlights (concise):
- Business SLO: conversational experience target = p95 latency <= 220 ms (end-to-end streaming chunk visibility) for 95% of interactive requests during peak traffic.
- Traffic shape: peak concurrency ~160 users, avg request ~120 tokens (prompt+expected response ~200 tokens), bursty 10-minute peaks.
- Streaming requirement: user must see first token within 130–150 ms; subsequent tokens streamed in ~30–50 ms chunks.
- Throughput target for canary: sustain 1.2M tokens/hour with <220 ms p95 overall (includes network & client-side chunking).

Primary cost/performance levers we'd evaluate:
1) Continuous batching: configure 40–80 ms batch windows on GPU pool to increase effective throughput while keeping tail latency near target. Expect 20–35% token-cost reduction versus single-request serving at similar p95.
2) Prefix/KV caching: warm KV cache for repeated system prompts & common instruction prefixes. We need a target cold->warm hit ramp (>=70% hit-rate after 10 minutes) — will measure cache hit-rate and cold-start penalty.
3) Quantization profiles: propose testing two profiles — int8 (balanced latency + quality) and 4-bit GFQ (fastest; minimal quality degradation for short responses). We'll produce perceptual-quality diffs on your eval set.
4) Model variants & fallbacks: primary serving on redwood-fast-7b for latency-critical paths; fallback to redwood-clarity-13b only when quality metrics require it (or for async batch jobs). Evaluate A/B for quality vs latency.
5) Streaming chunk size & decoder tuning: aim for 40–60 token chunks for tight first-token latency while keeping streaming network overhead manageable.

Proposed validation plan (48–72 hour canary):
- Phase A (warmup, 12 hours): ramp to 60% peak to warm KV caches and steady-state batching.
- Phase B (stress, 24–48 hours): run full peak profile including 10-minute bursts to stress autoscaling and batch windows.
- Metrics to gather: p50/p95/p99 token latency (end-to-end), first-token latency distribution, throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate, batch sizes distribution, model-level cost per 1M tokens.

Preliminary cost estimates (very rough):
- redwood-fast-7b + int8: ~$90 per 1M tokens served (with continuous batching & caching assumptions).
- redwood-fast-7b + 4-bit GFQ: ~$60 per 1M tokens (best latency).
- redwood-clarity-13b + int8: ~$180 per 1M tokens (higher quality fallback).
(We will produce a formal estimate after we run a 2-hour pilot.)

Asks / action items from Halo Health:
- Please upload a week of representative traffic (we requested halo_sample_traffic.json) and a small eval set (10–50 prompts you care about).
- Confirm the hard p95 target (220 ms) vs acceptable grace (e.g., 300 ms during 5% of peaks).
- Let us know preferred 48–72 hour window for the canary (we propose week of Nov 16).

Redwood action items:
- Marissa: create stress harness + initial config (batch window, cache policy, quant profiles).
- Ben: produce preliminary cost sheet and model latency projection by Nov 13 EOD.
- Grace: coordinate dedicated canary pool and draft SLO dashboard to share during run.
- Karthik: coordinate commercial ask (dedicated pool pricing) and confirm next call.

Attachments: halo_sample_traffic.json, halo_token_distribution.csv, redwood_estimate_v2.xlsx (attached as stubs).

Thanks again — we’ll move fast once you confirm traffic upload and canary window.

--
Karthik Iyer

Subject: Re: Halo Health — SLO qualification & stress test plan (batching / cache / quantization levers)

Karthik — thanks, this is extremely helpful and exactly what we needed to lock next steps. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: hard p95 target = 220 ms. Halo team can accept up to 300 ms for <5% of requests during extreme bursts, but we'd like to keep production SLO enforcement at 220 ms.
- Traffic: attaching the sample week (halo_sample_traffic.json) and a token distribution CSV. The producer team included a higher fraction of long-form summaries — ~12% of requests exceed 350 tokens.
- Streaming: first-token visibility is critical for perceived responsiveness. Our mobile UX times out animation after 250 ms, so the 130–150 ms first-token target you proposed is important.

We can do the canary week of Nov 16-18. We prefer the stress window to include one weekday peak and one weekend peak if possible.

Question: can Redwood run the pilot against both quant profiles simultaneously (int8 vs 4-bit GFQ) on parallel pools so we can compare quality metrics without impacting production? If so, we'll need a short A/B eval harness and a blinded quality review from our product team.

Attaching: halo_sample_traffic.json, halo_token_distribution.csv (sent as attachments).

Thanks —
Anna Lee
Head of Product, Halo Health
anna.lee@halohealth.com

Anna — we can absolutely run parallel profiles in isolated canary pools (int8 vs 4-bit) and produce blinded quality diffs. Technical notes and a few asks from infra: 

Technical plan (short):
- Create two isolated canary pools (canary-int8, canary-4bit) pinned to identical autoscale targets.
- Use continuous batching with adaptive windowing; start with 50 ms target batch window and allow dynamic shrink toward 30 ms if tail grows.
- Pre-warm prefix/KV cache using the first 2 hours of the Halo sample set; measure warm hit-rate and capture cold-start profiles separately.
- Streaming config: chunk-size 50 tokens, first-token priority enabled in the runtime scheduler.
- Telemetry: export token-level timestamps and per-request model selection tags (fast-7b vs clarity-13b) to the SLO dashboard.

A couple of practical asks from your infra team:
- Please provide an allowlist IP for the canary traffic so our private pilot pool can accept connections (or confirm you'll proxy through your existing test harness).
- If you have a small blinded quality panel, send the link to the evaluation doc we can use to collect ratings.

Ben and Grace — can you confirm cost estimate cadence? Ben, can you produce the 2-hour pilot estimate + delta across quant profiles by Friday (Nov 13)? Grace, please reserve a dedicated canary pool for Nov 16-18 and share the dashboard link once ready.

I'll draft the test-run config as a short YAML and drop into the shared Drive link.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
